articleTitle: Ultrasonography Validation of Condylar and Pre-Condylar Distances and its Correlation with the Arthralgia Intensity Attributed to Local Arthritis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) represent a prevalent form of musculoskeletal pain observed in individuals with chronic pain. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective therapeutic interventions, with imaging examinations playing a crucial role in assessing articular structures, as outlined by the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD). Given the significance of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) evaluation in dentistry, the integration of ultrasonography (USG) into clinical practice facilitates early detection of joint pathologies. This study aims to evaluate the correlation between condylar and pre-condylar measures to determine which more accurately reflects capsular expansion associated with intra-articular effusion and the intensity of arthralgia reported by patients in the future. Measurements of condylar and pre-condylar distances were conducted in a cohort of volunteers. The Spearman correlation coefficient between condylar and pre-condylar distances was determined to be 0.36. The results suggest a statistically moderate correlation between condylar and pre-condylar measures, indicating that the latter may serve as a potentially less biased and more valid screening tool for identifying capsular expansions attributed to intra-articular inflammation and associated pain in patients with TMD.

articleTitle: Elements of the Routine EEG Process for Beginners in a Hospital
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The electroencephalogram (EEG) is a test used to analyze electrical activity, evaluate, and diagnose various brain, neurological and psychiatric diseases. Performing the EEG exam efficiently requires technical, practical, and interpersonal skills from the specialist who performs it, which are not written anywhere for the hired intern. Therefore, the goal of this study is to provide essential support for the development of these skills. In developing the research, interdisciplinary knowledge of safety engineering, biomedical engineering, hospital engineering, and production engineering was applied, in addition to surveying the process of carrying out numerous outpatient EEG exams, also called routine EEG, and the entire context that the involves, through an internship at a neurology hospital. Thus, a concise consultation and training material was produced, which presents the factors involving the encephalography technician, the patient, the environment, and the equipment, in a hospital institution, but which can be applied in clinics, offices or even laboratories. The material developed combines rich and accessible content for beginners whose mission is to perform the EEG exam, with quality, safety, and reliability.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Probability of Acoustic Cavitation Induced by Focused Ultrasound with Short-Pulsed Emission
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Acoustic cavitation has been observed in various medical applications. Despite efforts to avoid it, there have been endeavors to utilize and regulate it. However, determining a parameter of this phenomenon has posed a challenge in understanding its characteristics. The present study focuses on the generation and detection of acoustic cavitation through ultrasound pulses of different durations and powers. An analysis of the obtained signals was conducted, highlighting the observed behavior and the probability of occurrence of the phenomenon in various experimental scenarios. Agarose phantoms with acoustic properties similar to water were used. The results revealed a significant relationship between the applied power, pulse duration, and the presence of acoustic cavitation, with a higher probability and duration of the phenomenon observed at higher power levels, over 80% in the highest power applied of 5W in short pulses of 10 and 30 μs. Additionally, it was identified that the initial pulse duration influenced in the early manifestation of the phenomenon. This study provides an understanding of acoustic cavitation and a possible development of itself in water-based phantoms. The findings presented here are part of an ongoing research aiming to develop effective methods for controlling and detecting this phenomenon.

articleTitle: Optical Detection of Acoustic Cavitation through Continuous Laser in a Controlled Medium Emulating Biological Tissue
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This study proposes an optical system for the detection of cavitation in a controlled medium, emulating current acoustic detection techniques. By using a high-intensity focused ultrasound transducer and a 530 nm wavelength laser, it aims to detect the presence of microbubbles generated by cavitation. The laser interaction with the bubbles causes an alteration in the light energy, enabling its detection. The capture of the altered laser light is carried out through an optical detection system that includes a photodiode with sufficient sensitivity to detect small particles. The application of ultrasound at a power level sufficient to generate cavitation can be detected by the reflected and refracted beams when a laser is incident within the phantom in the area where bubbles are generated. Variations in intensity on the order of 1.54% and 2.88% were recorded, reflecting the presence of cavitation and offering a perspective on the advantages in terms of resolution and ease of measurement for studying the optical phenomena of cavitation and its application for health benefits.

articleTitle: Features Characterization of Facial sEMG Signals for a Facial Paralysis Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Facial paralysis is characterized by sudden weakness or paralysis in the muscles on one side of the face, resulting in an asymmetrical facial appearance and difficulty performing normal facial movements, such as closing one eye or smiling. In this article our aim is to characterize the values of 5 features that describe 5 facial expressions in healthy subjects. To this end, signal processing is performed to find quantitative values for the facial expressions. From the calculated features, discrepancies of 3.55% to 23.35% were found between both sides of the face in healthy subjects for the smile facial expression. This algorithm will be integrated as a user interface for facial mapping and recovery follow-up in future work.

articleTitle: Time and Phase Shift Detection Methods to Estimate a Characteristic Speed of Sound/Temperature Rate of a Bilayer Phantom
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This study proposes the application of two signal processing methods to obtain speed of sound changes related to internal temperatures of a generic bilayer soft tissue phantom in the range of 25°C to 29°C based on temporal changes measurement from ultrasonic signals. The methods were calibrated using signals obtained from sunflower oil. Cross-correlation and phase shift were used to estimate this parameter, the former requiring subtraction of the accumulated delays in the deeper layer given by the upper layer. Values of Δt and flight times were obtained for each medium, as well as their linear regression on velocity. The average velocity change per degree Celsius was -1.4671 ms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/°C for fat and 2.0562 ms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/°C for soft tissue.

articleTitle: Routine EEG Process for Beginners using Geometry Compass Method in a hospital
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The electroencephalogram (EEG) is an exam used to evaluate the functional state of the brain and diagnose various cerebral, neurological, and psychiatric diseases. Performing the EEG requires technical and practical skills from the specialist who performs it, which are not written somewhere for a beginner in this professional practice. This project aims to present the methodology for marking EEG points in the International 10-20 System, using a geometric compass method that was tested in outpatient EEG exams, also called routine EEG, and showed considerable time savings. Therefore, this concise consultation and training material was produced, which presents the method step-by-step to help beginners in the profession carry out the EEG exam with quality and reliability.

articleTitle: Determination of the Volume that a Syringe Pump can provide for Fluids Injection into Nanochannels
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The injection of fluids through nanochannels is made using a microfluidic pump, for this specific application is needed that a non-commercial syringe pump can inject a minimum of 50 μL of fluids with density similar to distilled water. In this paper the design of a syringe pump and the determination of the minimum volume that can provide using a 1 mL syringe allows to deliver a volume of 30.75 nL per motor step, by changing the delays per step via software, the flow rate can be modified depending on the applications requirements.

articleTitle: Statistical Validation of the Use of Advanced Piezoelectric Sensors for the Measurement of Blood Flow in Coronary Transplants
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The use of coronary or bridge implants (by-pass) has been a great revolution in the advancement of methods for the treatment of coronary blood vessel occlusion. To evaluate implant quality, the most effective technique currently used is called Ultrasonic Transit Time (TTFM), however, reliability of measurements of very small blood flows in low-caliber arteries and veins still needs to be increased. The objective of this article is the evaluation of the piezoelectric sensors to be used a) to estimate the sensitivity of the sensors and b) to calculate the error of the prediction of the volumetric flow. Coupled to an electronic module capable of making measurements in the order of picoseconds. The results showed an uncertainty in the prediction of blood volumetric flow less than 5 ml/min. It is concluded that the sensors used in this research are comparable with commercial high-cost TTFM equipment in the international market.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Breast Tumor Visualization on MRI Based on α-Shapes
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Nowadays cancer is the leading cause of death worldwide, to determine the specific treatment for cancer tumors, it is common to get their 2D representation. To obtain a more accurate representation of the tumor a 3D model is used. In this paper a 3D reconstruction of all the models in the Breast Tumor Patient Models Repository, was made by using the a-shape technique. To generate the respective shape from every tumor model, the images were transform into point clouds considering the vertices and the central point of the voxels generated using different slices. The volume of each tumor obtained from this method was compared to the ones measured by five other techniques: stl model, the Trace method, the Frustum model, the convex hull method, and by counting the voxels quantity in every model. In 68% of the dataset the a-shape method had the best volume approximation, in 23% of it the best estimation was from the Trace method, and the Frustrum model was better for only 9% of the cases. The 3-D representations and the volume estimations are intended to be implemented in the planning of breast cancer treatment by microwave ablation, so it is necessary improve this process to provide trustworthy information.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Pixel Classification for Temperature Analysis in Ultrasonic Agar Phantom Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This study melds B-mode ultrasound imaging with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to pioneer non- invasive temperature monitoring in hyperthermia therapy, a critical advancement over traditional, invasive techniques. Leveraging the ALOKA ProSound 6 system, this work adapts ultrasound data to be congruent with the ResNet-50 CNN architecture, employing Ranklet transforms to elevate image quality for more nuanced analysis. The CNN, crafted with the deeplabv3plus architecture, is adept at segmenting ultrasound images into distinct temperature ranges, indicative of its potential in clinical hyperthermia applications. Despite achieving a high validation accuracy of 97.7%, the research identifies the constraints of a limited dataset and manual labeling, which may introduce biases in model generalization. These results, while robust, underscore the need for a more expansive dataset and refined labeling mechanisms to ensure the CNN’s efficacy and reliability in clinical scenarios. The study signifies a notable advancement in non-invasive thermal monitoring, paving the way for improved hyperthermia treatment strategies and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Evaluation of NOMA Systems for Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Mobile technologies are allowing the deployment of new health services such as teleconsultation, continuous patient monitoring or even remote robotic-assisted surgery. Many of these applications are built upon the new 5G wireless networks. One of the enabling technologies for these 5G networks is known as non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). This work shows a NOMA systems simulator that allows multiple users in real scenarios where interference cancellation among users is not ideal.

articleTitle: Genetic Programming for Feature Construction in Breast Ultrasound Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: We present a feature construction approach based on Genetic Programming (GP) for classifying breast tumors into benign and malignant cases on ultrasonography. GP is an evolutionary algorithm that codifies potential solutions in syntax trees, representing mathematical expressions that combine the inputs (i.e., morphological and texture features) using arithmetic operators and mathematical functions to construct new features that increase the descriptive power of the original ones. The experimental results show that the GP-based method achieves an accuracy of 87% with four constructed features. It is compared against two feature selection techniques, attaining 87% and 88% accuracy with 86 and 13 selected characteristics, respectively, and two deep networks proposed for breast ultrasound (BUS) classification, reaching 82% and 84% accuracy each. Thus, using a reduced feature set, the proposed method is an adequate alternative for distinguishing between benign and malignant breast tumors on BUS images.

articleTitle: In Vitro Degradation of Polydioxanone (PDO) Lifting Threads in Microfocused Ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Objective: Analyze the static degradation time of polydioxanone (PDO) threads with or without the association of microfocused ultrasound, which are techniques for aesthetic purposes. Materials and Methods: In vitro assays were conducted in isotonic solution using smooth polydioxanone (PDO) threads divided into 2 groups (n=3): FPL (Smooth Polydioxanone Thread) and FPLU (Smooth Polydioxanone Thread with Ultrasound). The FPLU group underwent microfocused ultrasound. Both groups endured the following analyses: UV spectroscopy Absorbance and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). Results: Absorbance by UV spectroscopy: The concentration levels of molecules in the aliquots showed that at 8 days both FPL and FPLU groups exhibited absorbance levels of 0.0040 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) and 0.00585 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>), respectively. At 30 days, these levels were 0.0799 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) and 0.0543 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>). At 60 days, the FPLU group showed significant increase to 0.2039 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) compared to the FPL group at 0.1152 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) reaching a degradation peaks at 60 days. At 90 days, the FPL group presented 0.1299 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) and the FPLU group presented 0.2377 (mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>/L.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>). SEM: Morphological differences were observed in both groups. Conclusion: FPLU group showed higher absorbance over time. Microfocused ultrasound accelerated degradation time PDO threads, diminishing its functionality.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Limb Tremor Caused by Parkinson’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Introduction: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a disease of the central nervous system that occurs because neurons do not produce enough dopamine, resulting in lack of coordination, rigidity, and limb tremor. Purpose: To use a device that quantifies the magnitude of dominant upper extremity tremor in a PD patient using electrotherapies as an adjunct to pharmacological treatment to document its impact on limb tremor and determine the concordance of its monitoring. Materials and Methods: clinical case of a patient with PD submitted to 10 sessions of electrotherapy. Tremor was quantified with the MPU6050 accelerometer and symptom progression was assessed with the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Scale. Results: Measurements with the instrument show a reduction in tremor of about 55% and on the scale, there was a reduction in the rating of motor symptoms of 4 units. Discussion: Electrotherapies are based on the inhibition of motor neurons which causes tremor to decrease because they do not perceive the signals sent by the central nervous system, so patients undergoing these therapies and drugs have an improvement in the motor symptoms of PD.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Movement Analysis Methodology for Validation of a Functional Electrical Stimulation Device in an Animal Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Functional electrical stimulation (FES) consists of applying low-intensity electrical currents to affected tissues to generate muscle contractions and movements in a controlled manner. FES-based therapy has shown notable benefits in the reeducation of movements and in the recovery of motor functions. We developed a non-invasive FES device to perform FES therapy. Being a medical device, a set of additional testing and validations is required to be used in a clinical setting. We performed a feasibility and safety test of the FES device to assist ankle dorsiflexion movement by stimulating the tibialis anterior muscle of a rabbit, a widely used animal model in muscle stimulation research. The aim of this work is to present a movement analysis methodology to assess the movements induced by the FES device in the tibiotarsal joint of the animal model. The protocol consists of 1) determining stimulation thresholds and applying 20 repetitions of FES while videorecording, 2) Videos are processed using a mesh to find vectors among frames that describe the trajectory and magnitude of the movement, 3) A Convolutional Neural Network is trained to classify individual video frames corresponding to dorsiflexion or rest, obtaining an average of 80% accuracy. This validates that FES generated by our device is effective and can evoke a functional movement.

articleTitle: Aspects to Take into Account in the Design ofUltrasonic Angiological Doppler Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Some of the main causes for which electrical noise is generated in ultrasonic angiological Doppler equipment are presented, mentioning their origins and characteristics. These can be of internal or external origin to the equipment, degrading their operation. The values of the impedance and phase module, corresponding to six Doppler sensors, and their incidence in the noisy behavior, according to the inductive or capacitive value of the impedance module for each one, are shown.In addition, the relationship between the bandwidth of the Analog Block’s receiver and the amplitude deformation (spectral composition) that occurs when the equipment operates in the pulsed mode of the Doppler signal is highlighted. Finally, it is presented as a compromise condition: "the lower bandwidth that guarantees the lower noise power at the output of the Analog Block’s receiver and at the same time, achieve the lowest deformation produced in the envelope of the pulse". Some additional recommendations are also suggested to mitigate noise.

articleTitle: Development and Measurement of Breast Tissue Mimicking Phantom with Medium and Low Adipose Content for Microwave Ablation Therapy Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common and deadly cancer among women worldwide. Microwave ablation (MWA) is a minimally invasive therapy that uses electromagnetic radiation to heat and destroy tumor cells. However, the effectiveness of MWA depends on the dielectric properties of the breast tissue, which vary according to the adipose content. In this work, we developed and measured two novel tissue-mimicking phantoms that represent high and medium adipose densities in breast tissue. We used a network analyzer and a dielectric probe to measure the complex relative permittivity and electrical conductivity of the phantoms in the frequency range of 2-4.5 GHz. We found that the phantoms had similar dielectric characteristics to the biological breast tissue reported in the literature. At 2.45 GHz, the high-density phantom had a mean relative permittivity of 54.2720 ± 8.6327 and a mean conductivity of 1.13972 ± 0.1811 S/m, while the medium-density phantom had a mean relative permittivity of 51.5931 ± 8.3708 and a mean conductivity of 0.8955 ± 0.1551 S/m. These phantoms can be used to evaluate and optimize MWA therapy for different breast tissue types, potentially improving the treatment outcomes for breast cancer patients with other adipose tissue densities.

articleTitle: Impact of the Cell-Spread and Ablation Imaging Technique on Irreversible Electroporation of MCF-7-seeded Hydrogels
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Tumor ablation may be achieved by irreversible electroporation (IRE) as a non-thermal, minimally-invasive procedure. Particularly, malignant breast tumors are an important tissue to target by IRE. This work presents MCF-7-seeded hydrogels as an analogue framework to in vivo tumors to evaluate the effects of IRE in breast cancer. The experimental ablation extent was imaged in a small surface (1.2 mm x 1.0 mm) in the center of the hydrogel by epifluorescence microscopy. The ablation extent in the complete hydrogels was solved through a computational model considering a homogeneous hydrogel surrounding a central block of MCF-cells heterogeneously spread within extracellular matrix. The electric field distribution revealed that 82% of the hydrogel undergoes more than 400 V/cm and is hence likely to achieve IRE. This distribution was contrasted against the experimental cell-death extent to determine the electric field threshold for IRE of MCF-7 cells as 549.16 V/cm (heterogeneous block) and 728.61 V/cm (homogeneous hydrogel) which are consistent with the values reported for liver, and pancreatic tumors in vivo.

articleTitle: Test Chamber for Particulate Matter Sensors Measurements in Controlled Environment Through a Python GUI
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The lifestyle of humankind in recent years has resulted in inordinate levels of air pollution. This has generated a trend in the design and manufacture of portable, personal and fixed-site PM monitoring systems to prevent exposure to air pollutants. However, these devices still need to be improved and properly evaluated to compete with environmental monitors on the market. In this work, a test chamber with controlled environmental conditions was developed for the evaluation of low cost portable and personal PM sensors. The developed system guarantees quick evaluation tests spanning from seconds to hours, to corroborate prolonged operation and correct calibration. It is controlled by a Python-based graphical user interface (GUI). The prototype ensures the recording of PM, altitude, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, luminescence, and temperature measurements. Thirty measurement tests were carried out to ensure robust performance and data transfer. Thereafter, three tests were conducted to measure PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> using burned wood smoke. In the aforementioned tests, Pearson correlation (r) analyses between two commercial PM personal monitors and a low cost PM test sensor were done. Rvalues over 0.98 were obtained in all the tests. This device could help evaluate the developed sensors to determine if the equipment meets appropriate calibration.
